# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Report: /app

## 1. Overall Structure

**What it is:** A **Flask-based REST microservice (Python) for Indian bank transaction enrichment/categorization** — the Dockerfile even names it `transaction-enrichment-python`. It accepts JSON arrays of parsed bank-statement transactions (description/narration, amount, type, balance, etc.), loads them into pandas DataFrames, and enriches them with `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `partyName` (payee/counterparty), PFM categories, and simple descriptions. Served via gunicorn on port 9898.

**Tech stack:** Python 3.9, Flask 1.1.2, pandas, numpy, fuzzywuzzy + python-Levenshtein (fuzzy name matching), scipy/scikit-learn (hierarchical clustering for salary/recurrence detection). Installed via `setup.py` (no requirements.txt, no README).

**Directory tree:**
```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/                  # pip package root
    ├── setup.py                        # deps: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, sklearn...
    └── categorizationapp/              # the actual package
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app creation, request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py               # 936 lines; routes + per-bank orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific categorizers (~5,300 lines)
        │   ├── HDFC.py  ICICI.py  SBI.py  Axis.py  Kotak.py  YES.py ...
        │   └── (Andhra, AuSmallFinanceBank, BOB, BOI, Bandhan, BankOfMaharashtra,
        │        Canara, Central, Citi, CityUnion, DCB, Federal, IDBI, IDFC, Indian,
        │        Indusind, Karnataka, KarurVyasa, PNB, Paytm, RBL, SVC, Saraswat,
        │        SouthIndian, StandardCharted, Syndicate, TamilnadMerchantile,
        │        UCO, UnionBank)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared enrichment logic (~5,800 lines total)
```

**HTTP API (in `Controller.py`):**
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — main enrichment endpoint. Payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`. Dispatches via a giant if/elif over bank name to `categorize_<BANK>_transactions(...)`, then chains: card_clean_names → card_purpose (credit cards) → purpose → clean_names → internal_payment → salary_detection (savings) → pfm_categorization → simple_description.
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — clusters transactions by partyName similarity.
- `GET /` — health check.

## 2. Enrichment / Categorization / Payee-Extraction Logic (exact paths)

### Stage 1 — Transaction category from raw narration (per bank)
`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` (35 files, one per bank). Each exposes `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` containing large `conditions_choices` lists of regex matches on `transactions.description` (+ amount/type constraints) resolved via `np.select`, producing `transactionCategory` values like `UPI`, `NEFT`, `ATM_WITHDRAWAL`, `REFUND`, `AUTO_PAYMENT`, `SALARY`, charges/penalty types, etc. **These same files also extract `partyName` and `party2`** from narrations using delimiter-splitting helpers (`sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_`, etc.) and `py_extract` regex capture, e.g. `HDFC.py` lines ~108–275. Largest/most representative: `Kotak.py` (327), `HDFC.py` (276), `Indusind.py` (263), `IDBI.py` (247), `ICICI.py` (245).

### Stage 2 — Sub-category ("purpose")
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — assigns `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, REIMBURSEMENT, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, INVESTMENT, CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, SHOPPING, etc.) for savings/current accounts from description/partyName/party2 regexes.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` — same for credit-card transactions.

### Stage 3 — Payee / counterparty clean names
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (1,971 lines) — the master merchant-name normalizer: maps raw partyName/description fragments to canonical merchant names ("Airtel DTH", "ACT Fibernet", "Adani Electricity", …) via `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` (927 lines) — credit-card variant, `card_clean_names(transactions)`.
- Raw extraction of partyName from narration itself happens in the BankScripts (Stage 1) using helpers in `AppUtil.py`.

### Supporting / downstream enrichment
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — shared regex constants (SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REP, CREDIT_CARD, SHOPPING, INSURANCE...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — bank-specific regex constants (e.g. `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC`, `HDFC_CLEAN1`).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` — `clean_input_df`, delimiter splitters (`sep_by_dash` etc.), `py_extract`, `fuzzy_match`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` — clusters credits by partyName (Levenshtein + scipy hierarchical clustering) to detect recurring salary.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` — flags self-transfers by fuzzy-matching partyName vs. accountHolder.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` — maps category/subcategory/merchantType into PFM buckets (`pfmCategory`: SHOPPING, BILL_PAYMENT, TRAVEL...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` — builds `pfmSimpleDescription` ("PartyName - Category label").
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py` — Levenshtein clustering to assign `Group_ID` for recurrent transactions.
- Enums (label display values): `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`.
- Orchestration: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`.

## 3. Tests

**There are no tests in this repository.** Verified via:
- No `test`/`tests` directories, no `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` files anywhere.
- Zero occurrences of `unittest`, `pytest`, or `assert` in the codebase.
- No pytest/tox/CI config files (no `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`, `.github/`, `Jenkinsfile`).
- The only "testing" references are commented-out dendrogram plotting blocks in `SalaryDetection.py` and `RecurrentTxns.py` marked "For testing purpose only".

**How you would run it (no test command exists):**
- Install: `cd categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .` (Python 3.9 recommended; pinned old deps: Flask 1.1.2, Werkzeug<2.1, Jinja2<3.1).
- Run app: `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (from `/app/categorizationapp`), or `python -m flask` equivalent via `categorizationapp/__init__.py` (dev server on :9898).
- Docker: `docker build -t enrichment . && docker run -p 9898:9898 enrichment`.
- If you add tests, `pytest` from `/app/categorizationapp` after `pip install -e . pytest` would be the natural convention; exercising logic requires POSTing to `/categorizeTransaction` or calling `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` / `purpose` / `clean_names` directly with a pandas DataFrame containing columns `description`, `amount`, `type`, `balanceAfterTransaction` (and `partyName`/`party2`/`transactionCategory` for downstream stages).

steps.message:
All four forum complaints plus the maintainer's repro traced to five one-token faults — each a boundary or structural offset inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the note predicted. Two files changed, 5 lines total.

## Fixes

**1. All-numeric reference credit no longer a cheque deposit** (mango_saver) — categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py:100
The rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` while its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 digits — the length gate made the rule dead, so rows fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. Neighboring HDFC remark rules (`^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$` at lines 214–215) confirm the field is 16 chars. Fixed to `eq(16)`.

**2. Bare-numeric salary credit lost its sub-tag** (mango_saver) — HDFC.py:124
The rule tested `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the canonical value everywhere else (Controller.py, Purpose.py, InternalPayment.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Indusind.py) is `"SAVING"` — another dead condition. Fixed the string.

**3. Leading direction word yields empty/wrong counterparty** (rk_ontheroad) — ICICI.py:159
`py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 — the direction word (`TO`/`FROM`) — instead of group 1, the name. "From" then got blanked by the downstream short-token cleaner, so the counterparty came back empty. Fixed to `index=1` (same convention as ICICI.py:168).

**4. Slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer lifts the numeric ref as payee** (auditlens) — ICICI.py:147
For `BIL/INFT/<numeric ref>/<payee>` (exactly 3 slashes), `sep_by_(description,2,3)` picked field 2 — the numeric reference — instead of field 3, the final payee field. Fixed to `sep_by_(description,3,4)`, consistent with the sibling rules (line 148 uses the last field for longer variants; line 206 shows the name lives at index 3).

**5. Offsetting credit recorded as bounce instead of reversal** (maintainer note) — HDFC.py:98
The debit/credit-pair reversal rule compared `description.eq(description.shift(periods=2))` — a structural offset. The identical rule in ICICI.py:49 and Saraswat.py:20 (and the companion bounce rule on the very next HDFC line) uses `periods=1`. With the mismatch, the REVERSAL rule never fired and line 99 caught the pair as `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`. Fixed to `periods=1`.

## Verification

- Synthetic single-row repros for all five cases failed before and pass after the fixes (e.g. 16-digit remark credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `123456` credit on SAVING → `SALARY` sub-tag, `TRFR TO:SURESH SHARMA` → `Suresh Sharma`, `BIL/INFT/001543210987/RAMESH KUMAR` → `Ramesh Kumar`, immediate offsetting IMPS credit → `REVERSAL`).
- No-regression check: a 28-row corpus of ordinary HDFC/ICICI shapes (UPI, NEFT, IMPS, POS, ATM, ACH, cheque, interest, salary, CMS, genuine auto-pay bounces, 5-field `BIL/INFT`) was labeled with the pre-fix code (`git stash`) and post-fix code — output is byte-identical, so nothing that was already correct changed.
